_purpose: Declarative stage gates. docs/scripts/readiness.mjs derives live status from features.json, architecture.json and sbom.cyclonedx.json and ticks each gate automatically. Edit THIS file to change what a stage means; do not edit the generated docs/readiness.json.

stages.name: Alpha
stages.definition: Works for its creator. Rough edges expected. No promises on data, security or stability. Testing is internal.
stages.exitQuestion: Can I demo this to myself without it falling over?

stages.name: Beta
stages.definition: Feature-complete for its stated scope and usable by external testers without the author present. Known limitations are documented, not discovered.
stages.exitQuestion: Can a stranger use this without me sitting next to them?

stages.name: General Availability
stages.definition: Reliable for paying customers. Automated quality gates, no build-time debt, real operational posture.
stages.exitQuestion: Would I put a paying customer's data in here and sleep?

stages.name: Enterprise Ready
stages.definition: Meets organisational procurement and security review. Identity federation, auditability, compliance evidence, contractual guarantees.
stages.exitQuestion: Would a security reviewer sign this off?

icps.name: Personal / solo use
icps.description: One operator, private deployment, data is theirs alone. Auth is optional because the deployment itself is the boundary.

icps.name: Team / shared beta
icps.description: A small group shares one deployment. Access control and reliable feedback become mandatory because users are not the author.

icps.name: Paid SaaS customers
icps.description: Strangers pay for reliability. Build hygiene, operational tooling and data portability stop being nice-to-haves.

icps.name: Enterprise procurement
icps.description: Sold into an organisation that must satisfy its own security and compliance obligations.

gates.label: Core CRUD loop works
gates.why: Without create, read, update and delete the product is a mock-up, not an app.

gates.label: Data persists beyond the process
gates.why: State must survive a restart, or the app is a toy.

gates.label: Users see failures instead of silent staleness
gates.why: The worst failure mode is one the user cannot see. A swallowed error leaves the UI confidently wrong, which destroys trust faster than a visible crash.

gates.label: No phantom features
gates.why: A feature that appears to work but silently does nothing is worse than an absent one. Absent is honest; phantom misleads the user and the next developer.

gates.label: Access control exists
gates.why: The moment a link is shared, anyone holding the URL has full read and write. Single-tenant-by-architecture is not access control.
gates.conditional: Not required for the personal ICP — a private deployment is its own boundary.

gates.label: The product works on the device it is used on
gates.why: A responsive layout that hides navigation on small screens is not responsive. It silently becomes desktop-only.

gates.label: Destructive actions are survivable
gates.why: Data loss in a productivity tool is unrecoverable by the user. Deletion must confirm, and must report honestly when it removed nothing.

gates.label: User input cannot alter query semantics
gates.why: Parameterised SQL prevents injection but not LIKE-wildcard semantics. Unescaped wildcards mean a search for '100%' silently matches everything.

gates.label: Automated tests exist
gates.why: Without a regression net every future change is an unverified gamble. This is the gate that makes the later gates affordable.

gates.label: Changes ship through a pipeline
gates.why: Manual deploys do not scale past one operator and do not gate quality. The pipeline is what makes 'it works on my machine' irrelevant.

gates.label: Third-party code is pinned and integrity-checked
gates.why: An unpinned CDN script executes whatever the vendor serves today, with full page privilege. Pinning with SRI makes tampering or accidental mutation detectable rather than silent.
gates.note: Satisfied 2026-10-17 by the build step: no CDN script tags remain at all, so every dependency is version-pinned through package.json and nothing is left to integrity-check at runtime. Google Fonts (DEP-008, DEP-009) still loads from a CDN but carries no script privilege; self-hosting the woff2 files is the remaining polish.

gates.label: No build work happens in the user's browser
gates.why: Runtime transpilation and runtime CSS generation mean the first paint pays for the build. It is also the reason an unpinned CDN script has to exist at all.
gates.note: Satisfied 2026-10-17. COMP-017 (the esbuild + Tailwind CLI pipeline) replaced COMP-008, COMP-009 and COMP-011, so this gate now tracks the health of the build pipeline rather than the absence of in-browser build components.

gates.label: Users can extract their data
gates.why: Data a user cannot leave with is data they do not own. Export is also the cheapest possible escape hatch for your own migration problems.

gates.label: Read paths are bounded
gates.why: An unpaginated SELECT grows with the dataset. What is fine at 50 rows is a timeout at 50,000, and it fails on the day it matters most.

gates.label: Federated identity (SSO/SAML/OIDC)
gates.why: Enterprises do not create separate credentials for every tool. No federation means no procurement.

gates.label: Audit log of who changed what
gates.why: An auditor asks who deleted the record. Without an audit trail the answer is a guess.

gates.label: Monitoring, alerting and a documented recovery path
gates.why: Enterprises buy the promise that someone will know before they do. An unmonitored system makes that promise falsely.

gates.label: Tenancy isolation is enforced, not incidental
gates.why: Isolation that relies on 'one deployment per customer' does not survive multi-tenancy, and does not survive a review that asks how you prevent cross-tenant reads.

gates.label: Documented compliance posture
gates.why: A security questionnaire arrives before the contract does. Answering it from scratch each time is how deals stall.
gates.note: Placeholder — no compliance artefacts exist yet (SOC 2 / ISO 27001 / DPA / sub-processor list).
